name: Lyo.FileSystemWatcher
tagline: Snapshot-based .NET file watcher. Finds creates, deletes, changes, moves, and renames with debounce and SHA256 hashing.
description: Snapshot-based .NET file watcher. Finds creates, deletes, changes, moves, and renames with debounce and SHA256 hashing.
features: **Snapshot-based change detection.** Compares directory snapshots rather than relying only on FileSystemWatcher events.
**Debouncing.** Batches rapid changes so an event storm does not fire.
**Hash-based move detection.** Finds file moves and renames even when the file system does not report them.
**Batch scan.** `ScanCompleted` fires once per debounce with the previous tree, current tree, and every detected change. `CurrentSnapshot` exposes the last completed tree.
**Thread-safe.** Safe to call from multiple threads.
**Options.** `FileSystemWatcherOptions` covers debounce, hashing, path comparison, subdirectory watching, and include/exclude regexes.
**Errors.** Snapshot and detection failures go to `Error`, and to `ILogger` when you pass one.

sections.title: File events
items: `FileCreated`. Raised when a file is created.
`FileDeleted`. Raised when a file is deleted.
`FileChanged`. Raised when a file's content is modified.
`FileMoved`. Raised when a file is moved to a different directory.
`FileRenamed`. Raised when a file is renamed (moved within the same directory).

sections.title: Directory change events
items: `DirectoryCreated`. Raised when a directory is created.
`DirectoryDeleted`. Raised when a directory is deleted.
`DirectoryChanged`. Raised when a directory's content changes.
`DirectoryMoved`. Raised when a directory is moved to a different parent.
`DirectoryRenamed`. Raised when a directory is renamed (moved within the same parent).

sections.title: General events
items: `OnAnyChange`. Raised for any file or directory change.
`Error`. Raised when snapshot or change detection fails.

sections.title: Event data
sections.body:
Every event carries a `FileSystemChangeInfo` object with these properties:

```csharp
public sealed record FileSystemChangeInfo(
    string? OldPath, // Previous path (null for created items)
    string? NewPath, // New path (null for deleted items)
    ChangeTypeEnum ChangeType, // Type of change
    bool IsDirectory, // True if directory, false if file
    int? OldFileCount = null, // Directory: files before change
    int? OldDirectoryCount = null,// Directory: subdirectories before change
    int? NewFileCount = null, // Directory: files after change
    int? NewDirCount = null) // Directory: subdirectories after change
```

sections.title: Metrics integration
sections.text: When `EnableMetrics` is `true` and an `IMetrics` instance is provided, these metrics are recorded:

items: `filesystemwatcher.snapshot.duration`. Duration of snapshot operations (timing).
`filesystemwatcher.snapshot.duration_ms`. Snapshot duration in milliseconds (gauge).
`filesystemwatcher.snapshot.file_count`. Number of files in snapshot (gauge).
`filesystemwatcher.snapshot.directory_count`. Directory count in the snapshot (gauge).
`filesystemwatcher.snapshot.item_count`. Total items in snapshot (gauge).

`filesystemwatcher.changes.detected`. Changes detected per scan (gauge).

sections.title: Error handling
File hashing
items: **Enabled (default).** Accurate move/rename detection. Slower against large directories.
**Disabled.** Faster. Move detection relies on file system events only.

sections.title: Memory usage
items: Snapshots keep the complete directory tree in memory
For very large directory structures (10,000+ files), consider these:
Disabling file hashing
Increasing debounce delay
Monitoring memory usage

sections.title: Debounce delay
items: **Lower values (50-100ms).** Faster response, higher CPU usage.
**Higher values (500-1000ms).** Slower response, lower CPU usage.
**Default (250ms).** A reasonable default for most directories.

sections.title: Expected snapshot times
items: **Small directories (< 100 files).** Under 100ms per snapshot.
**Medium directories (100-1000 files).** 100-500ms per snapshot.
**Large directories (> 1000 files).** 500ms+ per snapshot. Hashing large files stretches that further.

sections.title: Thread safety
Disposal
Events are not firing
items: **Check path exists.** The directory must exist when the watcher is created.
**Check permissions.** Read access to the directory is required.
**Check debounce delay.** Very rapid changes may be batched.
**Check event handlers.** Subscribe before changes occur.
**Wait for initial snapshot.** The watcher needs time to take that first snapshot.

sections.title: CPU is high
items: **Disable file hashing.** Set `EnableFileHashing = false`.
**Increase debounce delay.** Higher values reduce CPU usage.
**Watch snapshot frequency.** Too many rapid changes can spike CPU use.

sections.title: Memory is high
items: **Watch snapshot size.** Large directory trees consume more memory.
**Disable hashing.** Reduces memory per file entry.
**Dispose the watcher.** Leaks show up if it is left running.

sections.title: Move/rename events are missing
items: **Enable file hashing.** Needed for reliable move/rename detection.
**Check the file system.** Some file systems never report move events.
**Check timing.** Very rapid moves may show up as delete+create.
**Directory moves.** The directory name must stay the same (new parent, same name).

sections.title: Known limitation: file move bug
sections.text: There is a known bug: directory change events for the source directory when moving a file show incorrect counts. The destination directory works correctly.

sections.title: Known limitations: performance
items: File hashing can be slow on large files or on many files
Snapshot operations are synchronous and can block for a moment
Very large directory structures consume significant memory

sections.title: Known limitations: directory move detection
items: Directory move detection only works when the directory name stays the same and the parent changes
If both name and parent change, it is detected as delete + create

sections.title: Architecture: snapshot-based detection
sections.text: The watcher takes periodic snapshots of the directory tree and diffs them. That is more reliable than FileSystemWatcher events by themselves.

sections.title: Architecture: debouncing
sections.text: A debounce timer batches multiple rapid changes, which prevents event storms and reduces CPU usage.

sections.title: Architecture: hash-based move detection
sections.text: File hashing (SHA256) detects moves and renames even when the file system does not provide that information directly.

sections.title: Architecture: error resilience
items: Event handler exceptions are caught and logged, so one faulty handler cannot crash the watcher
Snapshot errors are caught and reported through the Error event
Cancellation tokens allow graceful shutdown of long-running operations

sections.title: Types
rows: Snapshot-based, debounced watcher (`IDisposable`). Constructor: `FileSystemWatcher(string path, FileSystemWatcherOptions?, ILogger?, IMetrics?)`. Raises the file/directory/`OnAnyChange`/`ScanCompleted`/`Error` events listed above.
`record` payload emitted by every change event.
In-memory snapshot of the watched tree, used for diffing.
One event per debounce with previous tree, current tree, and the full change list. `CurrentSnapshot` is the last completed tree.
`ToDto()` extensions that copy size/timestamps onto persistable models (relative '/' paths).
Metric and tag name constants (snapshot, change detection, event, and error metrics above).
